thread:
Maya Lin: Quick heads-up — noticed an inconsistency in the /generate examples. The curl example mentions an `X-Prefetch: true` header that changes server prefetch behavior, but the Python and Go SDK snippets don't show how to opt into prefetch. Users reported different latency/cost expectations. Can we align the examples?

Alex Kim: Good catch. I remember we added the header as an internal optimization flag. It should be documented as optional and shown how the SDKs set it.

Sam Ortiz: Hmm — do we actually want to advertise `X-Prefetch`? Might encourage people to toggle without understanding tradeoffs. Maybe we should call it out as "advanced" or behind a runtimes flag? 

Maya Lin: Agree we should surface tradeoffs. Minimal ask: make the curl + SDK samples consistent and add a one-line note about what prefetch does (reduces token-level latency for warm prefixes, can increase cost if misused).

Priya Patel: I can update the docs PR. Which file is the canonical sample? I found docs PR #3245 with the curl example but the python snippet in that PR is older. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3245

Alex Kim: @Priya Patel that PR is the one. Thanks. For SDK snippets, show both automatic behavior and explicit header override. Example for Python: `client.generate(..., prefetch=True)` if available, otherwise show `headers={"X-Prefetch": "true"}` for raw REST. For Go show `req.Header.Set("X-Prefetch", "true")`. Keep the simple example first.

Maya Lin: Suggested copy for the note: "Prefetch (advanced): when enabled, the server will attempt to pre-initialize KV cache for repeated prefixes which can improve latency for interactive workloads. It may increase upstream compute for short-lived requests — use with evals or traffic experiments." Short and link to runtime doc.

Sam Ortiz: +1 on keeping it 'advanced'. Also suggest we avoid implying it's required for streaming; it's orthogonal.

Priya Patel: I'll push a tiny PR with the following changes: 1) update curl example to keep `X-Prefetch` but mark as optional; 2) add Python & Go snippets showing both automatic param and raw header; 3) add the short note and a pointer to the runtime docs page. Draft commmit msg: "docs: clarify prefetch header and align SDK snippets (curl, python, go)"

Docs Bot: Noted. Please reference the docs style guide when adding code blocks and inline params (https://redwood-inference.internal/docs-style).

Alex Kim: One formatting detail — use inline code for header names (``X-Prefetch``) and show minimal working examples. For Python snippet, use the official SDK call pattern we ship in examples:```python
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood()
resp = client.generate(model="rwd-3b", prompt="hello", prefetch=True)
print(resp.text)
``` For curl, show:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Prefetch: true" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"hello"}'
```

Priya Patel: Great — I'll include both code blocks. Any objections to adding one sentence about cost tradeoffs?

Sam Ortiz: Add it but keep it non-prescriptive. Maybe: "Enabling prefetch can slightly increase per-request compute for small prompts; measure in your workload before enabling globally."

Maya Lin: Perfect. Once Priya sends the PR, can someone from runtime review to make sure we didn't misstate the behavior? @Alex Kim can you take that?

Alex Kim: Yep, I'll review runtime semantics and confirm phrasing. If there are breaking changes, I'll call out.

Priya Patel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3280 — small changes, added tests for example rendering. PTAL @Alex Kim @Maya Lin

Docs Bot: PR 3280 checks passed (lint + examples render).

Alex Kim: Reviewing now. Found one nit — in the Go snippet we should prefer `GenerateRequest` pattern used in the SDK 2.x examples. I'll comment on the PR with a replacement snippet.

Priya Patel: Thanks, pushed the Go snippet update. Anything else?

Maya Lin: No other blockers. Thanks all — once merged, I'll add a short note in the release notes for the docs changes (docs: note prefetch examples alignment). :tada:

Sam Ortiz: Awesome. One follow-up: can we add a quick test case in our examples harness that renders both variants to catch regressions? If not now, add issue for follow-up.

Priya Patel: Adding issue #5422 to track examples harness test for header variants.

Docs Bot: Issue #5422 created by Priya Patel.

Maya Lin: Great work, team. Closing thread after PR merges.
